title: Foundation-1 procedure-proof test times out its 10s hook under full-suite load
description:
`packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/foundation1ProcedureProof.test.ts`
fails with `Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms` when run as part of the full
Vitest suite, and passes (43/43) when its file is run alone.

INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED AS PRE-EXISTING, 2026-09-12: reproduced on a clean
detached checkout of `origin/main` at `67e0653` with no other changes —
`npm run test` there reports `1 failed | 296 passed | 2 skipped`, the same
file, the same hook timeout. It arrived with PR #545 / the Foundation-1
importer stage, not with PR #543.

WHY IT MATTERS
It is a false red on the pre-commit gate and on `main` itself. An agent that
takes it at face value either chases an unrelated change or learns to ignore a
failing gate.

LIKELY CAUSE (unverified)
A `beforeAll`/`beforeEach` hook that builds or loads importer output. Under
full-suite load (one worker per file) that work exceeds the default 10s hook
timeout; alone it does not.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in preference order
1. Raise the hook timeout for that file to reflect the real cost of the setup
   it performs. The assertions are about procedure projections, not speed.
2. Hoist the shared setup so it is paid once per suite rather than per hook.
3. Only if neither holds: give the file a dedicated pool.

Do NOT fix it by skipping the file or weakening its assertions — it is the
permanent evidence for the Foundation-1 procedure-projection work.

RELATED
A sibling pre-existing flake is filed for
`packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs` (same shape: a
10s timeout under full-suite load, green standalone).
notes:
2026-09-14 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 / PR #546): root-caused and mitigated. The beforeAll hook reads the multi-MB SRD PDF and extracts every page; measured isolated cost is ~3.5s (3.63s, 3.49s over two runs), so vitest's default 10s had under 3x headroom against parallel workers. It went from intermittent to DETERMINISTIC (three reproductions, including one with a single worktree and more free RAM than an earlier passing run of the same base - the opposite of a transient-load signature) once PR #546 added ~23 pack-loading and discovery tests to the same run. Hook budget raised to 60s (~17x measured isolated cost) with the measurement recorded in-line. No assertion changed: a timeout bounds how long an expensive I/O fixture may take, not what counts as correct, and a genuine hang still fails. If a durable fix is wanted, the real lever is caching the extracted pages across the importer test files that each re-extract the same PDF.
2026-09-22 RE-EXAMINED under the 6-worker cap (eshyra-9l5s.2 / PR #552) by eshyra-9l5s.5. VERIFIED CAUSE: worker fan-out contention (Vitest default maxWorkers = availableParallelism() = 20 on a 7.8 GB host with swap ~91% used at idle), per audit docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md section 2. EVIDENCE (measured, not 'did not reproduce'): a temporary timing probe in the beforeAll hook (reverted; tree verified clean) recorded 2,817 / 2,895 / 3,222 ms across three capped full-suite runs, against 2,356 ms with the file alone. Load inflation under the cap is 1.2-1.4x, so even vitest's default 10 s would have >=3.1x headroom; the 60 s budget has ~19x. Nine capped full-suite runs this session were green. DISPOSITION: fixed at the cause by the worker cap. The 60 s hook budget from 473424d is KEPT deliberately rather than reverted: it bounds an expensive I/O fixture, not correctness, a real hang still fails, and CI runners (cap 4, slower CPUs) have not been measured for this hook. Reverting it would buy no protection. The page-extraction caching lever in the prior note is not warranted by the measurement: the file is ~1 s of in-suite time.
close_reason: Cause verified (uncapped worker fan-out) and fixed by the worker cap from eshyra-9l5s.2; hook measured at 2.8-3.2 s under the capped full suite vs 60 s budget. Evidence in notes (eshyra-9l5s.5).
